A free local analysis and evidence-assessment product for applications, compiled libraries and header-only libraries. Explainable maintenance assessment, versioned configurable policies, trustworthy context-bound external-tool/test/coverage/runtime evidence, installed CLI/build/editor/agent workflows, bounded scale, maintainable extensions and repeatable candidate/release processes. All M0–M9 remain comparison scope; M8/M9 are explicitly expansion/optional outcomes and require their own sub-specifications, rather than prerequisites for the first useful release.

Working hypothesis: help C++ library/header-only maintainers know which declared compiler/OS/target/standard/macros/options have current applicable verification, what failed and what is unknown; help consuming applications identify what upstream evidence does not cover. Reuse compilers and established tools, bind their facts to actual distributed artifacts, distinguish health/ranking/completeness/policy status. User demand and comparative advantage remain unvalidated.

The focused discovery says it does not authorize the broader backlog or rewrite TASK_SPEC. It preserves the broader proposal. Therefore neither the broad specification nor the focused hypothesis can silently erase the other; later user authorization changes execution scope, and this audit must compare with the full proposal while identifying unresolved product choices.

conflicts.finding: Historical D8/D13/architecture say default executes 15 detectors and MISRA is opt-in. Current engine variant contains all 22 and current DECISIONS explicitly explains profile only changes scoring/roadmap. Uploaded discovery already identified discrepancy.

conflicts.requirement_or_topic: Large/header-only libraries versus fixed size skip
conflicts.finding: Safety style requires skipping >500KB and the analyzer still has a hardcoded 500*1024 cap. Production design forbids a hardcoded small limit excluding common amalgamated libraries and requires configurable explicit limits. Current skip is recorded, so it does not silently fabricate analyzed scope, but the supported library use remains incomplete.
conflicts.remaining_work: Replace fixed cap with configurable resource/large-file policy and isolated bounded work; test an actual >500KB distributed header including positive/negative triggers and an exhausted/incomplete case.

conflicts.requirement_or_topic: C++17 style requirements versus later-language APIs and historical assertions
conflicts.finding: C++ style mandates C++17 while recommending std::expected; safety rules recommend std::span, require public expected/noexcept and assert mutex aggregation/TSan. The standard APIs are unavailable in C++17 without alternatives and source instruction text is not evidence that thread safety or TSan passed.
conflicts.remaining_work: Reconcile style around C++17-supported alternatives and actual worker design; preserve explicit failure statuses, validate callbacks/error paths and run appropriate sanitizer/compiler matrix before claiming support.

conflicts.requirement_or_topic: Public CLI design versus implemented interface
conflicts.finding: Design proposes text default, init --kind, config show --effective, collect --recipe, installed CMake find_package function with ANALYZE_TARGETS and check changed flags. Current CLI uses machine JSON stdout, init --repo, config flat form, collect --request/workspace/store and snapshot check semantics. These can be deliberate strict interfaces but are not the same contract.
conflicts.remaining_work: Perform command-by-command compatibility/UX reconciliation. Supply documented text default and aliases where required, or propose explicit versioned contract changes. CMake collection and retained-snapshot checking need a clear end-to-end recipe, not a claim that checking automatically collects.
